distortions.title: Cognitive Distortions
distortions.subtitle: Learn to recognize distorted thinking patterns in your own thoughts.

letGo.placeholder: Write down the thought that's bothering you
letGo.hintQuestion: Sounds like {{distortion}} — what would you say instead?
letGo.dragHint: Drag the card away to let it go

allOrNothing.definition: Seeing things in only two extremes — perfect or a total failure — with no middle ground.
allOrNothing.example: "I made one mistake in the presentation, so the whole thing was a disaster."
allOrNothing.reframe: "One part didn't go perfectly, but most of it went well — that doesn't erase the rest."

overgeneralization.definition: Taking one negative event and treating it as a permanent, never-ending pattern.
overgeneralization.example: "My friend didn't text back — nobody ever wants to talk to me."
overgeneralization.reframe: "One person being busy right now doesn't mean this always happens."

mentalFilter.definition: Picking out a single negative detail and dwelling on it so much that your whole view of the situation darkens — like a drop of ink coloring an entire glass of water.
mentalFilter.example: "The meeting had one awkward moment, so the whole thing felt like a failure."
mentalFilter.reframe: "Most of the meeting actually went smoothly — I'm zooming in on the one rough moment."

discountingPositive.definition: Insisting that your good qualities or achievements don't count.
discountingPositive.example: "I only did well because the test was easy, not because I'm capable."
discountingPositive.reframe: "I prepared for this and it paid off — that's a real accomplishment."

jumpingToConclusions.definition: Assuming you know what others think (mind reading) or predicting the worst outcome (fortune telling) without evidence.
jumpingToConclusions.example: "She looked at her phone during our chat — she must think I'm boring."
jumpingToConclusions.reframe: "I don't actually know what she was thinking — there could be many reasons."

magnification.definition: Blowing problems out of proportion, or shrinking your own strengths down to nothing.
magnification.example: "I forgot one detail in the report — this could ruin my whole career."
magnification.reframe: "It's a small error I can correct — it's not going to define my career."

emotionalReasoning.definition: Assuming your feelings reflect the facts: 'I feel it, so it must be true.'
emotionalReasoning.example: "I feel like a failure, so I must actually be one."
emotionalReasoning.reframe: "Feeling like a failure right now doesn't mean I am one — feelings aren't proof."

shouldStatements.definition: Criticizing yourself or others with rigid 'should,' 'must,' or 'ought to' rules.
shouldStatements.example: "I should never make mistakes at work."
shouldStatements.reframe: "I'm allowed to make mistakes — that's how people learn and improve."

labeling.definition: Attaching a harsh, global label to yourself or someone else based on one incident.
labeling.example: "I missed the deadline — I'm such a failure."
labeling.reframe: "I missed one deadline — that's a single event, not who I am."

personalization.definition: Blaming yourself for events that were largely outside your control.
personalization.example: "My team missed the target — it must be entirely my fault."
personalization.reframe: "Many factors contributed to this — I'm not the only cause."

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.operatorText: Personal data is processed by the operator of Moodly: Individual Entrepreneur Stepanova K.S., address: [address], INN: [INN], OGRNIP: [OGRNIP]. Official contact email: privacy@moodly.app.
privacy.legalBasisText: Processing is based on: (a) your consent given at registration, including consent to the processing of special category data concerning mental health (Article 9 GDPR / Article 10 of Russian Federal Law No. 152-FZ); (b) performance of the contract (terms of service) to which you are a party (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR); (c) legal obligations.
privacy.dataWeCollectText: We process data you voluntarily provide: email address, birth year, mood and symptom entries, psychological test results, journal entries, breathing session logs, and technical information about push notification subscriptions. Data concerning your psychological state constitutes special category data (GDPR Article 9 / Article 10 of 152-FZ) and is processed only with your separate explicit consent. We do not process data beyond the purposes stated in this Policy.
privacy.howWeUseText: Your data is used solely to provide Moodly's core functionality: mood tracking, test scoring, practice recommendations, personalized insights, and service notifications. We do not sell your data or use it for advertising. Aggregated, anonymized statistics may be used for product improvement.
privacy.dataSharingText: We do not share your personal data with third parties except: (a) with your explicit consent, (b) when required by law, or (c) with service providers who process data on our behalf (hosting providers, email service) under data processing agreements. Each provider is contractually bound to confidentiality and security.
privacy.crossBorderText: Personal data of Russian citizens is stored and processed in databases located on the territory of the Russian Federation. During development and testing, certain technical operations (hosting, sending service emails) may involve foreign services. Such transfers are carried out in accordance with Article 12 of 152-FZ and, where required, with separate consent and prior notification to the supervisory authority.
privacy.dataRetentionText: Your data is retained no longer than necessary for the purposes of processing: while your account is active. On account deletion, consent withdrawal, or fulfillment of the purposes, personal data is destroyed within 30 days unless retention is required by law. You may request deletion of your account and associated data at any time via the Settings page.
privacy.securityMeasuresText: The operator appoints a person responsible for data processing and implements legal, organizational, and technical measures: encryption in transit (TLS), password hashing, access control, logging, and monitoring. The measures comply with Article 32 GDPR and Articles 18.1 and 19 of 152-FZ.
privacy.yourRightsText: You have the right to access, rectify, block, export, and delete your personal data, and to withdraw your consent at any time without stating a reason. To exercise these rights, use the Settings page or contact us at privacy@moodly.app. On withdrawal of consent, processing stops; data processed before withdrawal is retained only to the extent and for the periods required by law.
privacy.responseTermsText: The operator responds to data subject requests within 10 business days of receipt (Article 20 of 152-FZ). The deadline may be extended by no more than 5 business days with written notice to the data subject. Refusals are accompanied by a reasoned response within the same period. You may appeal the operator's actions to the supervisory authority or in court (Article 17 of 152-FZ).

terms.limitationOfLiabilityText: Moodly is provided 'as is' without warranties of any kind. To the maximum extent permitted by law, the operator shall not be liable for any damages arising from the use or inability to use the service.

meta.title: Sleep hygiene: how sleep affects mood and anxiety
meta.description: Simple sleep hygiene rules: regularity, light, screens and relaxation. Learn how to improve sleep and wellbeing.

hero.title: Sleep hygiene
hero.accent: how sleep affects mood and anxiety
hero.text: Lack of sleep directly affects mood, energy and anxiety. Simple habits help you sleep better within days.

item.1: Go to bed and wake up at the same time
item.2: Keep the phone out of bed

why.title: Why sleep matters
why.text1: Sleep restores emotions and energy. Poor sleep fuels irritability and anxiety.
why.text2: Tracking sleep alongside mood makes the link easier to see.

1.title: Mood
1.text: When sleep-deprived, even small problems feel bigger.

2.title: Energy
2.text: Sleep quality determines your charge for the whole day.

3.title: Anxiety
3.text: Enough sleep helps you respond to stress more calmly.

1.title: Regularity
1.text: Go to bed and wake at the same time, even on weekends.

2.title: Light
2.text: Dim bright lights in the evening, especially before bed.

3.title: Screens
3.text: Avoid the phone or laptop right before sleep.

4.title: Caffeine
4.text: Limit caffeine and energy drinks in the afternoon.

5.title: Relaxation
5.text: Breathing or a thought journal help you slow down before bed.

6.title: Dark, quiet, cool
6.text: Your bedroom should be dark, quiet and cool.

how.title: How Moodly helps you sleep better

1.title: Track your sleep
1.text: Log sleep quality alongside mood in 30 seconds.

2.title: See the link
2.text: Trends show how sleep affects your state.

3.title: Practice
3.text: The “sleep hygiene” practice with reminders helps build the habit.

1.q: How many days until sleep improves?
1.a: First changes often appear within a few days of regularity. Consistency matters more than perfection.

2.q: Should I keep a sleep diary?
2.a: Yes. Logging sleep and mood reveals patterns you can't see by eye.

3.q: Is this a substitute for a doctor?
3.a: No. It is a self-help tool. For persistent sleep problems, see a professional.

cta.title: Improve sleep and wellbeing
cta.text: Start tracking sleep and mood — and notice what really helps.

disclaimer.1: Moodly is a self-assessment and self-help tool, not a medical service.
disclaimer.2: If you have persistent sleep problems, see a doctor.

1.text: Slow breathing eases tension in the moment. Moodly has a guided timer.

2.title: Thought journal
2.text: Write anxious thoughts down — they often lose their power when spoken.

3.title: Gratitude
3.text: A few notes of gratitude each day gently shift focus away from threat.

4.title: Sleep hygiene
4.text: Sleep directly affects anxiety. Get your sleep routine in order.
